Les titulaires s’engagent à exécuter les prestations avec tout le soin en usage dans la profession. Il s s’engagent également à mettre en œuvre tous les moyens nécessaires à la bonne exécution des travaux qui lui sont confiés. Les titulaires devront s’équiper du matériel nécessaire en quantité et en qualité pour assurer la fabrication et la livraison des supports dans des conditions satisfaisantes et sont soumis à une obligation de résultats. Les qualités de disponibilité, de réactivité et d'adaptation aux contraintes de délais stricts seront requises pour l'imprimeur. Le prestataire devra dans son offre désigner explicitement un interlocuteur et joindre un pouvoir signé d'une personne habilitée donnant à cet interlocuteur les pouvoirs nécessaires au respect de cet engagement. The potential of the Wroclaw agglomeration for the development of the Industry 4.0 sector is vast; thus the entire ecosystem should continue working together to nurture and develop it. The city-business- science triad has a long tradition in Wroclaw, so the intensification of joint activities can bring even more new effects in a short period of time. 7 This connection can help us to build a strong Industry 4.0 sector able to compete with similar ecosystems in Europe and worldwide. This report clearly demonstrates that the community of Wroclaw is ready to pursue this goal. Dr Magdalena Okulowska President of the Wroclaw Agglomeration Development Agency (ARAW) THE RATIONALE FOR THIS REPORT Is Wroclaw a reasonable choice to place an Industry 4.0 investment? T o meet the business needs of today’s manufacturing companies, a location should provide an environment ready and open not only for slow-moving change but clearly – for an industrial revolution. It seems that before the pandemic, the Wroclaw agglomeration had everything in place to welcome Industry 4.0 with open arms. However, COVID-19 has surely affected this scene and its members. Examples of such activities include adding green spaces, making it easier to get around the city and provide better access to health care – all goals of Wroclaw’s strategy for 203017 backed by the city and the EU funding for projects. Many data points show that these efforts are bearing fruit. The metropolitan area of Wroclaw is growing, with now over 2 million people living within an hour’s drive. Foreigners are also entering the local job market, with almost 61,00018 of them registered in the state social insurance (ZUS) system. More importantly, businesses are taking advantage of the improvements. A 2019 survey19 showed that 82% of large IT corporations in Wroclaw chose the city because of the access it gave to qualified workers. In the case of international production companies, this rate can reach even higher. All respondents in the digital industry study pointed to the availability of skilled labour as a crucial factor behind their decision to launch an investment in Lower Silesia20. PRODUCT PERSONALISATION AND SERVITISATION The ability to create more product variants while using the same resources is crucial to building a competitive advantage. That’s why increasing production flexibility has long been a pressing matter for manufacturers. Again, data is the game-changer here. Processing real-time information at all stages of user interactions enables creating product simulations that can be adapted to match unique, individual requirements of the customer. Similarly, many manufacturing businesses now expand the value for their clients by shifting from selling products to selling Product-Service Systems (PSS). Pioneered in the 1960s by Rolls Royce, servitisation relieves customers of capital costs, instead offering them advanced solutions in a subscription model. 16 PLATFORMISATION OF PRODUCTION Just as products are now increasingly offered as a service, the manufacturing process is also subject to similar changes. ON INDUSTRY 4.0 WORLDWIDE Before the outbreak of COVID-19, there was widespread interest in Industry 4.0. The sector’s value was projected to grow up to $3.7 trillion by 20259. However, despite these positive outlooks, the actual landscape of Industry 4.0 adoption has been far more complex. ASPIRATIONS VS REALITY 90% of respondents in McKinsey’s10 annual survey admitted seeing the benefits of digital transformation in manufacturing. A majority of them included introducing new technologies as an essential part of their organisational development strategies. However, as research from the World Economic Forum11 demonstrates, despite these declarations, the reality was still far from this ideal. In 2018, the adoption of technology in production still remained slow across industries and regions. ip_data_security.text: This change wouldn’t be possible without advancements such as the Internet of Things (IoT), the Cloud, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), or Artificial Intelligence (AI). 13 Therefore, this publication follows the BCG’s definition of Industry 4.01, seeing it as a transformation that enables analysing data across machines and using it for more efficient manufacturing at reduced costs. CORE TECHNOLOGIES SUPPORTING INDUSTRY 4.0 Autonomous robots & cobots Digital Twins & simulation The AI-powered cloud Augmented & virtual reality Digital integration systems The Industrial Internet of Things Additive manufacturing Big Data & analytics Cybersecurity * ORGANISED AFTER THE BOSTON CONSUL TING GROUP Apart from increasing productivity, Industry 4.0 also encourages developing new products and business models. As a result, it modifies the workforce profile and reconfigures the competitiveness of companies and regions. These issues will be discussed later on in this chapter but first, let’s focus on the three core advancements differentiating Industry 4.0 from the previous revolutions. DATIFICATION Integrating data from devices, sensors, and IT systems enables developing new solutions at all stages of the product lifecycle – from design to production, logistics and maintenance. 1

ntinuously collecting, analysing, and using data in real-time. IIoT enables monitoring of all production processes and scheduling maintenance accordingly. When integrating Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Customer Relationship Management (CRM), the network allows for comprehensive management of all related operations. THE CONVERGENCE OF IT SYSTEMS AND OPERATIONAL TECHNOLOGY (OT) In the past, IT and OT worked as separate entities: the first one mostly serving management, the latter controlling machines and resources. Thanks to the IIoT, these two worlds have been increasingly converging. Cyber-physical systems (CPS) embody this tendency as machines now combine both the IT and operational qualities. One of the most advanced CP systems – Digital Twins – enables creating digital replicas of physical objects but also processes based on data collected from sensors. ROBOTISATION AND AUTOMATION Industry 4.0 is also underpinned by a growing level of robotisation and automation. Apart from automated production lines, factories now boast autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and collaborative robots (cobots). ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

 

The con

responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

aneku esitamine ja olekumuudatused; varustuse muutmised ja varustuse broneeringud; teavituste saatmine (kinnitus, meeldetuletus, tagasiside); teenuse lõpetamine ja tegelike näitajate muutmine; arve genereerimine/saatmine/staatusmuutus; PDF-tõendi genereerimine ja allalaadimine; integratsioonipäringud (nt Moodle) koos veateatega. 8.2 Auditlogi väljad asutus, kasutaja/roll, tegevus, objekt (tüüp ja ID), ajatempel, tulemus, tehniline jälg (nt request-id). 8.3 Säilitamine (retentsioon) Auditlogide säilitamise miinimum: 3 aastat automaatse arhiveerimisega. Täpne retentsioon ja ligipääsuõigused lepitakse kokku projekti käigus ning kooskõlastatakse GDPR nõuetega. 9. Juurutuse miinimumnõuded 9.1 Tehniline paigaldusviis Rakendus on konteineriseeritud (Docker). Juurutus kirjeldatakse docker-compose või Helm lahendusena. Tarnitakse paigaldusjuhend (install, update, rollback). 9.2 Konfiguratsioon (keskkonnamuutujad ja saladused) Minimaalne konfiguratsioon jaguneb kaheks: Keskkonnamuutujad (mitte-salajane): avalikud URL-id, asutuste nimed/valikud, e-posti saatmise lülitid, logitase. Saladused (secret): OIDC client_secret’id, Moodle tokenid, e-posti SMTP paroolid, krüptovõtmed. Saladused ei tohi olla lähtekoodis; hoitakse turvalises secrets-lahenduses. Saladusi ei tohi hoida Docker-compose failide

Brändiraamat sisaldab vähemalt järgmisi osi: Brändi alused: brändi olemus ja identiteet; sihtrühmad; brändi positsioneering; missioon, visioon (on ette antud hankija poolt) ja brändi lubadus, mille lõplik sõnastus kinnitatakse projekti käigus. Verbaalne identiteet: kommunikatsioonistiili kirjeldus (tone of voice); keelekasutuse põhimõtted; peamised sõnumid; kommunikatsiooni kehahoiak; näited erinevatele sihtrühmadele. CVI juhendi logoperekond: Tallinna Haigla logo eesti ja inglise keeles; Tallinna Kiirabi logo; Tallinna Hambakliiniku logo; logo koos laiendi või tunnuslausega; logo kasutamisel erinevates geograafilistes tegevuskohtades; logo kasutamise reeglid; värvisüsteem (Pantone, CMYK, RGB HEX süsteemides): primaar-, sekundaar- ja tertsiaarvärvid; aktsentvärvid; värvikombinatsioonid; tüpograafia; tunnusgraafika; kujunduse üldpõhimõtted (sh logode kasutus positiivis, negatiivis ja must-valgena, keelatud kasutusviisid, minimaalsed mõõdud jne); Ikoon. Illustratsioonid, foto- ja videokeel: illustratsioonide stiil; foto- ja videokeel, sh inimeste, haigla keskkonna, seadmete kujutamine; tunnusgraafika kasutamine fotodel ja videotes; kompaktne kujunduskontseptsiooni visualiseering, sh valgus, värvilahendused,

s, värvilahendused, emotsioon, keelatud fotostiilid. Väärtustega seotud piktogrammid: inimkesksus; professionaalsus; usaldusväärsus. Scope of Work The contractor shall only print and mail paper copies of the Judiciary W-2 and 1099-R, 1099-INT, 1099-MISC, and 1099-C Forms for calendar years 2026-2031. The forms will be printed on paper from PDF data files provided by HRO and FMO and mailed to the correct recipient as directed by the Judiciary. All supplies and equipment for printing and mailing the tax forms other than the AO’s USPS bulk mailing permit shall be provided by the contractor. The contractor shall mail W-2s and 1099 forms to address in the Continental United States (CONUS), Outside of Continental United States (OCONUS), as well as to U.S. territories and international a

The contractor must have the capability to securely receive and store electronic files from the AO using AO approved encryption methods such as Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) for files in-transit and hard disk encryption for files at-rest. The contractor shall make available their secure file system for remote AO security testing and inspection by the AO DCIO Information Assurance Branch immediately after award, and prior to any work performed under this contract. In the event the contractor’s system is deemed incapable of performance, and the contractor is unable to fully comply with the requirements to securely receive and store electronic files from the AO, the results shall be relayed to the AO Department of Administrative Services (DAS) Acquisition Management Office (AMO) for potential contract action, to include immediate termination.
